newsitem.title: FRANCE: Frenchman snared in paedophilia net kills self.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman snared in paedophilia net kills self.

text.p: A man snared in France's biggest ever crackdown on paedophiles committed suicide on Thursday after being questioned about pornographic materials found in his home, police officials said.
The man, a postal inspector in his 40's from the eastern town of Saint-Martin-d'Heres, was found hanged in his home, where he had left a suicide note, police officials said.
Police had searched his home on Tuesday and questioned him after finding the pornographic materials, they said.
The man was among 634 people rounded up across the country in the police swoop, which began on Tuesday.

Of those, 204 have been formally placed under investigation on suspicion of "handling images from the crime of corruption of minors aged under 15". Being placed under investigation under French law is short of an indictment but is a first step towards a trial.
Prosecutor Jean-Louis Coste said some of the hundreds of videos seized were "unbearable" and had provided evidence of 11 cases of rape.
One video showed a teenager in an act of bestiality. Another showed one of the detainees raping four minors.
The raids followed 14 months of investigation which led the gendarmerie to a mail-order company in the central town of Macon selling pornographic films involving boys.

The operation -- dubbed "Ado 71" after the French word for teenager and the car registration figure for the Macon region -- involved some 2,500 gendarmes across mainland France as well as on the French Caribbean islands of Martinique and Guadeloupe.
